name: Maldives
summary_text: Maldives is dangerous for trans visitors — a sharp resort/local split. Under the Penal Code and sharia framework, same-sex conduct is criminalised (up to 8 years, with 100 lashes available), and gender-nonconforming Maldivians face prosecution and social erasure; activists operate from exile (a 2024 HRC shadow report documents ICCPR violations). BUT: the tourist resort islands operate as a legally distinct world — no LGBT tourist is documented as prosecuted on a resort; the risk concentrates in Malé and local islands. A resort-only visit is lower-risk than the score suggests; any local-island contact raises it.

sources.claim_summary: Kaleidoscope Human Rights Foundation alternative report to the UN Human Rights Committee (June 2024) on the Maldives' protection of LGBTQI+ rights under the ICCPR: prepared with local activists - documents legal and social context, evidence and testimony of rights violations, and ICCPR provisions potentially violated. Same-sex conduct is criminalised in the Maldives with Sharia-based penalties.

Human Rights Measurement Initiative Maldives 2024 summary: expert survey data - LGBTQIA+ people are among the groups most commonly identified as at risk of violations of empowerment rights; low scores on freedom of religion/belief (1.8/10), assembly (4.1) and expression (4.7).

US State Department 2020 Human Rights Report for Maldives: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised under the 2014 Penal Code and Sharia; significant societal stigma; no LGBT-specific protections.

sources.title: Maldives: Lenient no more, island nation arrests 2
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (Sept 2015): 'Maldives: Lenient no more, island nation arrests 2' - two men (56 and 27) arrested in their private home on Dhaandhoo for homosexual activity; the 2014 Penal Code extended criminalisation beyond Muslims to everyone, potentially punishable by death; Rainbow Warriors warned tourists could face similar threats.

UN OHCHR compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/22/MDV/2, March 2015) for the Maldives' 2nd-cycle UPR: treaty-body and special-procedures information including reservations to ICCPR/CEDAW/CRC and human-rights concerns.

Maldives national UPR report (A/HRC/WG.6/22/MDV/1, April 2015): the government's own submission - development achievements, the 2014 Penal Code, and its handling of first-cycle recommendations (89 accepted, 20 rejected).
